question: What is the difference between a single discount of 48% on ₹1,450 and two successive discounts of 10% and 40% on the same amount?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Successive discount of 10% and 40% = 10 + 40 − (10 × 40) ÷ 100 = 46%.

Single discount = 48%.

Difference in discount percentage = 48% − 46% = 2%.

Difference in amount = 2% of ₹1,450 = (2 ÷ 100) × 1,450 = ₹29.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹29.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → **Marked Price (MP)** = ₹1,450, **Single Discount** = 48%, **Successive Discounts** = 10% and 40%.
Formulas: Successive Discount = a + b − (ab ÷ 100) | Discount Amount = (Discount% ÷ 100) × MP.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/38b40b7c3f5595b938bb75e348ea88e8654121de5f026e25b146d76388133d12.png] 
⇒ **Discount 1** (Single) = 48% of 1,450 = 0.48 × 1,450 = ₹696.
⇒ **Effective rate** for successive discounts = 10 + 40 − (10 × 40 ÷ 100) = 50 − 4 = 46%.
⇒ **Discount 2** (Successive) = 46% of 1,450 = 0.46 × 1,450 = ₹667.
⇒ **Difference** = ₹696 − ₹667 = ₹29.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹29.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discounts

When two or more discounts are applied one after another on the **Marked Price**, they are called successive discounts. The formula for two successive discounts a% and b% is [a + b − (ab/100)]%.

Marked Price vs Selling Price

**Selling Price (SP)** = Marked Price × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100. The discount is always calculated on the **Marked Price** unless stated otherwise.
